verdicts.reason: A reads well from left to right (brand, product, headline, CTA), but the 'Longest Day Sale' badge is shrunk to an unreadable sliver and the legal text is nearly as large as the subline. B puts the CTA first, before the headline, so the reading order is backwards; the sale badge is a tiny sticker jammed against the end of the subline, and the oversized legal block on the far right competes with the logo.

A has effectively lost the product (it is a speck), leaves the SOLSTICE logo nearly invisible in a dead middle gap, and the sale badge is a tiny fragment colliding with the CTA's right edge. B keeps the product and logo visible, but it leads with the CTA before the headline, the sale badge is illegibly small next to the subline, and the legal text is too prominent.

B has a sensible left-to-right order (badge and product, headline, CTA on the right) and a clear hierarchy, but the SOLSTICE logo is a dark-on-dark speck, the badge is very small, and the legal text sits heavy under the subline. A puts the CTA ahead of the headline, wedges the sale badge in tiny after the subline, and gives the legal text too much weight on the right.

B buries the CTA: 'Claim the Deal' is a tiny pill under a large red sale banner that outranks it, and the logo is an invisible speck beside it, so the hierarchy is inverted. A has a prominent CTA and a readable logo, but its order runs CTA then headline, the sale badge is illegibly small and jammed against the subline, and the legal text is oversized.
